newsitem.title: USA: NTN auditors doubt its ability to continue.
newsitem.headline: NTN auditors doubt its ability to continue.

text.p: NTN Communications Inc said Wednesday its auditor, KPMG Peat Marwick LLP, had issued an opinion expressing doubt about the company's ability to continue.
In a statement accompanying its 1996 earnings report, NTN said the auditor cited the company's recurring losses from operations and its net working capital deficiency.
NTN said it has already implemented an organizational and strategic restructuring aimed at substantially reducing overhead and focusing on its core business.

It said this involved a workforce reduction, a buyout of certain high-cost lease commitments, and a restructuring of management personnel and responsibilities. It said the workforce reduction included five senior officers.
NTN said management believes these steps will contribute toward achieving profitability and improving cash flow.
NTN today reported a loss of $22.95 million for the full year 1996, compared with a loss of $3.95 million for 1995. Revenues rose to $25.7 million from $20 million.
The 1996 loss included charges related to a strategic restructuring and a previously announced executive management reorganization.

NTN said it continues to experience significant problems with its equipment at sites in restaurants, taverns and other hospitality locations throughout North America. It said the problems contributed to significant customer disconnects in the 1996 fourth quarter and 1997 first quarter.
